findings.rule: git switch, add, commit and push only for the review branch and the review directory.
findings.input: Bash command `git stash` with no arguments
findings.finding: A bare `git stash` (which defaults to `git stash push` and mutates the working tree) is treated as an unconditionally allowed read subcommand because GIT_WRITE_FLAGS.stash only matches specific sub-arguments like `push` or `pop`, so the argument-less form is never denied even though it is not the branch/add/commit/push exception the rule names.

findings.rule: git switch, add, commit and push only for the review branch and the review directory.
findings.finding: The `add` check allows any path where `path.includes(run.dir)` is true rather than requiring the path to be inside the review directory, so a path that merely contains `reviews/spec-fidelity-sonnet` as a substring of a different directory name is staged without denial.

findings.rule: Bash is allowed only for read commands (git read subcommands, cat, sed, grep, find, ls and the like), no python, no node, no test runner, no redirections.
findings.finding: `mkdir` and `touch` are added to the Bash read-command allowlist with a scoped write exception, even though the rule restricts Bash to read commands and names no directory- or file-creation exception.
